# The Keeper of Forgotten Names

In the time before memory, there lived a crane who nested at the edge of the world, where the sea meets the sky. This crane, called Memoria, possessed a peculiar gift: she could hear the names of all things as they faded from existence.

When the last speaker of an ancient tongue died, their words would drift like seeds on the wind to Memoria's nest. When a species vanished from the earth, she would catch its true name in her beak. When a star collapsed in the distant heavens, its celestial title would fall to her like rain.

Memoria wove these forgotten names into her nest, thread by thread, creating a tapestry of all that had been lost. The nest grew vast, shimmering with the ghosts of extinct flowers, abandoned gods, and languages that once sang across continents.

The other birds asked why she bothered collecting such sorrowful things.

"Because," Memoria replied, "nothing truly ends if someone remembers it began."

To this day, when you recall something you thought you'd forgotten, or when a word sits just beyond your tongue's reach, it is Memoria singing from her nest, reminding the world of all it has loved and lost.

The Sun, envious of this gift, tried to cry as well. But his tears were too hot and evaporated before reaching the ground, creating only mist and fog. Frustrated, the Sun demanded the Moon stop crying, claiming it made him look weak by comparison.

The Moon, heartbroken by her brother's jealousy, agreed. But the night flowers began to wither without her tears. The earth grew parched in darkness.

Seeing the harm caused by his pride, the Sun apologized. They made a pact: the Moon would cry her silver tears each night, and the Sun would warm them each morning, creating the eternal cycle of dew and evaporation.

Thus, the siblings learned to work in harmony, each gift completing the other.
